transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Cho (Redwood AE), Samir Verma (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood Solutions), Priya Raman (NexaHealth Head of ML), Ethan Mills (NexaHealth SRE), Laura Kim (NexaHealth Security), Omar Ruiz (Product)

Summary:
High-level scoping for POC benchmark integration. Focus areas: harness integration, customer-provided scripts, load testing parameters, streaming vs non-streaming runtimes, success criteria (latency, throughput, cost, quality), timeline for a two-week pilot leading to decision.

Topics:
- Benchmark harness integration and handoff
- Workload sizing and representative scripts
- Streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs
- Success criteria and pass/fail thresholds
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Cho: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda, we want to line up the benchmark harness, see how your scripts plug in, define workloads and success criteria. Priya, can you give a 30-second on what success looks like for NexaHealth?
[00:18] Priya Raman: Yeah hi thanks. for us it's three things, one is latency for interactive features — p95 sub 500ms ideally, two is cost per 1M tokens must be under our target which I think we said around $45, and three is output quality measured by our clinical slot-level accuracy on the eval set, no more than a 2% regression vs current model. also security and data residency are non-negotiable.
[00:41] Samir Verma: got it. quick clarifying question, Priya: is the 500ms target for streaming responses or end-to-end non-streaming? because those have different baselines.
[00:50] Priya Raman: primarily streaming, that's how the product is architected, we stream partial summaries and then finalization. we will also test non-streaming batch workloads but streaming is the priority.
[01:04] Ethan Mills: and from infra side we care about sustained throughput, e.g. 300 concurrent users, which maps to approx 120 rps for the summarization endpoint. we also want to see behavior under spikes up to 800 rps.
[01:16] Alex Cho: perfect, that's helpful. Samir, high level on the harness - what do we expect to run on their side vs Redwood side?
[01:23] Samir Verma: so our benchmark harness is a small runner that can execute either our Redwood load profiles or customer scripts. typical integration options: 1) customer supplies native scripts (python/golang) that call Redwood SDK/REST, we wrap them into our harness and run in their VPC via an agreed runner, or 2) we provide a turnkey harness where we push workloads from Redwood's infra. either way we capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, throughput (rps), error rates, and tail noise under different batch and cache settings.
[01:51] Omar Ruiz: for customer scripts, we mostly have internal orchestration in k8s and a small API shim; so ideally we give you a script and config and you run it in our staging. is the harness containerized?
[02:01] Samir Verma: yes harness is containerized. we provide a docker image and a small runner. customers can run it in their k8s cluster with a service account. we also have a lightweight remote agent option if you prefer Redwood to orchestrate under a limited window.
[02:15] Laura Kim: security question — if you run the harness in our cluster, what network requirements and creds are needed? we need SAML auth, and KMS support for keys, ideally no long-lived secrets.
[02:26] Maya Patel: we do short-lived tokens and support customer-managed KMS for payload encryption. we can present the security design in a doc. We'll also provide SOC2 and audit logs.
[02:35] Priya Raman: great. what about streaming vs non-streaming tuning — are there separate kernel/quantization implications?
[02:42] Samir Verma: yes. streaming favors smaller per-request latency and smaller token-chunking; we keep KV cache warm and avoid large batching. non-streaming batch runs can push higher batching to reduce cost per token but increase latency. for quantization, our profiles recommend int8 for batch, q4/ q8 variants for low-latency streaming depending on model. note: in transcripts sometimes we say 'KV cash' by mistake but it's KV cache.
[03:09] Ethan Mills: can you capture cold-start behavior? during spike tests we don't want a 2-3s cold start if it causes user-visible blips.
[03:16] Samir Verma: yes we test cold start and warm steady state. we'll run step traffic (ramp) and pulse traffic for spike behavior. we'll record warmup time to p95 and token-generation stability.
[03:26] Alex Cho: let's talk metrics and pass/fail thresholds. Priya already gave a baseline. we usually propose acceptance criteria: p95 streaming latency < 550ms (allows buffer), error rate < 0.5% on 24h window, quality regression < 2% on your labeled eval set, and cost per 1M tokens within 20% of target. any objections?
[03:47] Priya Raman: that's reasonable. we'd prefer hard p95 < 500ms but can accept 550ms in demo then tighten in pilot.
[03:55] Omar Ruiz: can we get a breakdown by token types? we have long-prompts vs short-prompts.
[04:01] Samir Verma: yes harness will run three profiles: short (avg 60 tokens in/out), medium (avg 250), long (avg 1200) — we'll capture tokens generated, latency per chunk, and effective tokens/sec.
[04:13] Alex Cho: timeline — what's realistic for a POC? we usually do a 2-week pilot: week 0 set up harness and alignment, week 1 run functional/quality tests and small-scale perf, week 2 run full load and cost analysis, then debrief. any constraints?
[04:28] Priya Raman: timing looks fine, except we go into holiday freeze Dec 24-26. so need to do heavy lifting before Dec 24 or push to Dec 28 for load window.
[04:37] Alex Cho: we can aim to ship harness and docs by 12/23 and schedule the big run on 12/28 as discussed in next steps.
[04:44] Laura Kim: one more on data: the sample dataset will contain PHI. we need an air-gapped runner option or a runner that never sends data to Redwood-managed infra.
[04:54] Maya Patel: we support VPC/private deployment for the POC and an on-prem runner; the harness can be configured to never exfiltrate logs and to encrypt payloads with your KMS. we'll add the exact config to the security doc.
[05:06] Ethan Mills: operationally, we want the runner to emit Prometheus metrics and a CSV/JSON output for post analysis. can the harness do that?
[05:13] Samir Verma: yes it exposes Prom metrics and produces structured artifacts (CSV/JSON) plus a link to raw traces. also we produce a result sheet with p50/p95/p99 and cost breakdown by model variant, batch size, and quantization.
[05:26] Priya Raman: and on the quality checks, we will run our labeled eval set for regression detection. does the harness support automated eval hooks?
[05:33] Samir Verma: yes you can plug in your evaluation script; the harness will run them post-run and attach the results. we also have a small evaluation runner for A/B comparison across model versions.
[05:45] Omar Ruiz: curious about model variant fallback — we sometimes want automatic fallback to a cheaper equiv during capacity spikes. is that supported in the harness?
[05:53] Alex Cho: yes at serving layer we support routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible variants; for benchmarking we can emulate the fallback behavior or disable it to measure worst-case.
[06:03] Priya Raman: Costs — can we get an estimate for our expected monthly usage if pilot scales? rough math: 100k monthly summaries at avg 250 tokens output.
[06:12] Alex Cho: we'll run cost sims in the post-run sheet; Samir will include cost per 1M tokens for streaming and batch profiles for your numbers.
[06:20] Ethan Mills: do we need to sign any additional contracts to run the harness in our infra?
[06:24] Maya Patel: usually an MSA addendum specifying limited access for pilot; we can run under a standard POC agreement and a PA for SOC2 needs. Laura will review.
[06:33] Alex Cho: ok let's recap next steps and who does what.
[06:36] Alex Cho: Alex sends harness README and sample scripts + pricing matrix by 12/23.
[06:40] Samir Verma: Samir prepares Redwood config templates for streaming/non-streaming runs and quantization profiles by 12/27.
[06:45] Ethan Mills: Ethan provides sample dataset and workload profiles by 12/24.
[06:49] Laura Kim: Laura returns security questionnaire and confirms KMS requirements by 12/23.
[06:55] Priya Raman: We'll review and confirm the 12/28 benchmark window.
[06:59] Alex Cho: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to docs and the meeting notes.

End of transcript.
